column1: There are definitely other design choices that impact how easy it is to write valuable tests, rather than ending up with tests where every dependency is mocked—which are a pain to write, a nightmare to maintain across refactorings, and a huge time sink with almost no value. Good unit tests cover the public interface using real code, relying only on minimal fakes for the lowest external layers like network transport or platform API calls. Because these tests verify expected outcomes rather than specific internal implementations, they survive internal refactorings and can be used without rewrites to verify that the refactoring was done correctly.","I had a case that nearly motivated me to switch my team's project (a 1M+ line codebase) from MVVM to MVI or another pattern to address recurring boilerplate, where MVI seemed to offer clear benefits. In the end, though, we solved it all elegantly using Kotlin's delegation pattern, and MVI's perceived benefits disappeared."
